description:
FILED s468be (Opus) while attributing the companion ROW DIFF (178 NEW / 407
FIXED, measured on f330e5f).  PRE-EXISTING; the instrument, not the product.

THE MECHANISM.  baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv (I1) keys a row on
(rel, PERL's description) and compares it as a MULTISET.  Four files build
their descriptions out of perl's own hash state, which is randomised per
process (PERL_HASH_SEED):

  op/hash.t     "0 .. 9 (+2) uses >0 heads (6)", "a .. zz copy has >0 array
                size (32)" â the bucket-head and array-size counts.
  op/undef.t    "$key: keys|values|each 1|delete|each 2" where $key is
                whichever X::DESTROY perl runs first over %hash
                (t/op/undef.t:84-105) â "k1: delete" one run, "k2:" the next.
  op/utfhash.t  "\w on keys with 3 keys, key of length 4" â BOTH sides
                interpolate their own keys/each order, so the description
                PAIRING itself is a different draw each run.
  op/inc.t      "key '2' incremented correctly" / "key '0' decremented
                correctly" â t/op/inc.t:112-127 iterates `keys %inc` and
                `keys %dec` and interpolates the (in|de)cremented key, so
                which of the four rows fails to pair is a per-run draw.

MEASURED, not deduced â four runs of ONE tree (s466 validate1, s466
validate2, the s468be serial run and the s468be bless run, all on 9bee19b's
emission):

  op/hash.t     45/45, 57/57, 46/46 NEW/FIXED; 486 diverging rows every time,
                59 of them different between the last two.
  op/undef.t    14/14 throughout; 3 of 55 rows differ between two runs.
  op/utfhash.t  18/20, 11/19, 0/32; the diverging-row COUNT itself was
                51 (blessed) / 43 / 19.
  op/inc.t      2/2, 2/2, then 4/4; 36 diverging rows in three runs, 40 in
                the fourth (both key spellings unpaired at once).

The ok/not-ok COUNTS are stable in all of them (8/7, 33/4, 91/0, 62/13), so
the count snapshot (baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv) and the shortfall (I2) still
gate these files; only the row multiset stands down.

op/inc.t was nearly missed and is the lesson: its rows were IDENTICAL in two
consecutive runs, so it was on course to be blessed â and the very next run
produced a third draw.  TWO AGREEING RUNS ARE NOT EVIDENCE OF A STABLE ROW
SET IN THIS FAMILY.

WHAT WAS DONE (s468be).  The `*rows-unstable*` opt-out that
baselines/perl-suite-expected-rows.tsv has carried since s336
(mro/package_aliases_utf8.t) and s399 (op/assignwarn.t â the same cause,
`keys %should_warn`) was extended to I1: a file whose blessed rows are exactly
one `*rows-unstable* <cause>` entry opts out of the ROW check and keeps that
entry through a `--bless-fails`.  run-perl-suite.pl gains
`fails_rows_unstable`, one line in bless_fail_rows and one in report_row_diff,
which NAMES every opt-out file on every run so the opt-out is never silent.
Guard: tools/t/audit-instruments.t â including a check over the REAL baseline
that an opt-out entry is never sitting beside ordinary rows, which would be a
silent no-op.  592 + 40 rows left the row gate this way.

WHAT WAS **NOT** DONE, and why â the alternatives, each with its measurement:

 (a) A description NORMALISER in the row-key builder.  Measured: rewriting
     `uses >0 heads (\d+)` -> `(N)`, `k\d+:` -> `kN:` and
     `with \d+ keys, key of length \d+` takes op/hash.t 57/57 -> 2/2 (the
     residue is a THIRD token, "has >0 array size (32)"), op/undef.t 14/14 ->
     0/0 and op/utfhash.t 11/19 -> 0/8, and does NOTHING for op/inc.t, whose
     volatility is in the row ALIGNMENT rather than the key text.  REJECTED:
     those are per-FILE test prose, not a token class, so they would put three
     files' wording into a reader shared by both row baselines.  The one
     pattern that IS a class â t/test.pl's PID-derived tempfile name, perl's
     own $::tempfile_regexp â WAS added (it fixed op/require_errors.t's 4 rows
     permanently) and is the boundary.
 (b) `PERL_HASH_SEED=0 PERL_PERTURB_KEYS=0` in the environment of the PERL
     ORACLE child only.  This would make every description in the family
     deterministic and is the durable fix, but it changes what the oracle
     measures (op/hash.t is a test OF hash quality) and is a decision about
     the suite's contract, not a bless.  NOT MEASURED here.
 (c) A per-file registry of description normalisers.  More machinery than the
     opt-out for the same result.

RESIDUE / WHAT TO DO NEXT.  If (b) is ruled acceptable the four registrations
come straight back out and 632 rows return to the gate.  Until then these four
files are gated by COUNTS only â that is the cost, and it is named on every
run.  Before adding a fifth member, measure at least THREE runs (see op/inc.t
above).

ONE PROPERTY OF THE OPT-OUT, noted so nobody rediscovers it as a bug: a
registered file can never go STALE the way an XDIFF registration does â if its
rows all stopped diverging the entry would just sit there.  What catches that
is the COUNT snapshot (baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv): a file whose verdict goes
DIFF -> OK is a snapshot mover and is reported.  The same is true of
perl-suite-expected-rows.tsv's registrations, so this is the family's existing
behaviour, not a new hole.


=== s469bf (2026-09-05, Opus) — THREE MORE MEMBERS, and the volatility measured
=== at the SOURCE instead of inferred from repeated companion runs ===

While attributing the s468 full-companion ROW DIFF of the re/ comp/ run/ dirs
(199 NEW / 74 FIXED), three more files turned out to be this family.  All three
have COUNTS identical to their snapshot in every run and a row multiset that is
a per-run draw:

  re/regexp_unicode_prop.t   t/re/regexp_unicode_prop.t:223
                             `while (my ($class,$chars) = each %SHORT_PROPERTIES)`
                             builds %d AND the @CLASSES list.
  re/pat.t                   t/re/pat.t:434 `for (keys %ans)` — the sixteen
                             `20000 nodes, {const,var}-len '<key>'` rows.
  re/pat_advanced.t          t/re/pat_advanced.t:119
                             `while (my ($code,$match) = each %d)` — the twelve
                             `Properties of \x{7f,80,ff,100}` rows.

A CHEAPER AND STRONGER MEASUREMENT THAN REPEATING THE COMPANION RUN.  The
volatility is entirely in the PERL ORACLE, so it can be measured with no SBCL
at all: run perl's own file three times and compare the TAP description
SEQUENCES.  (`scratch/s469bf/perlorder.sh` + `ordercmp.pl` in the s469bf
worktree; ~10 seconds a file.)

  re/pat.t                  3 x 1188 rows — order DIFFERENT in every pair,
                            multiset SAME; first divergence at row 270 (the
                            `20000 nodes` block).
  re/pat_advanced.t         3 x 1675 rows — order DIFFERENT, multiset SAME;
                            first divergence at rows 29-32 (`Properties of \x..`).
  re/regexp_unicode_prop.t  3 x 1110 rows — order DIFFERENT, multiset SAME;
                            first divergence at row 244 (`qr/\p{Lo}` vs `qr/\p{Cc}`).

  TRAP while doing this: compare the multisets under LC_ALL=C.  A locale-
  collating `sort | uniq -c` splits byte-identical descriptions across groups
  and reports a false "multiset DIFFERENT".

THE COMPANION DRAWS that follow from it, all on ONE tree (main c80b1a0), all
with COUNTS equal to the snapshot:

  file                      s468 --all   s469 --dir re   s469 alone   counts
  re/regexp_unicode_prop.t  149/51       80/38           161/42       778/332 x3
  re/pat.t                  8/12         8/6             8/12*        231/138 x3
  re/pat_advanced.t         3/6          3/6             6/3          951/729 x3
  (* a different key set from s468's, same totals)

  re/pat_advanced.t is the op/inc.t trap again: the FIRST TWO RUNS AGREED
  (3/6 with the identical rows) and the third drew `Properties of \x80` instead
  of `\x7f`.  Three is the minimum, and this family keeps proving it.

THE TRUNCATION AMPLIFIER (#1051) — new, and it is why the registration has to be
the WHOLE file and not the volatile block.  re/pat.t and re/pat_advanced.t both
exceed the 500-row log cap.  The volatile block sits EARLY in each file (rows
277-292 and 29-36), so a different draw changes how many rows the 500-row window
consumes and the window's right edge moves — re/pat.t's last paired row went
718 -> 722, re/pat_advanced.t's 1186 -> 1189.  Rows at the edge then read as NEW
or FIXED with nothing about them changed: re/pat.t's four
`(?il), utf8=…, locale=…` rows and re/pat_advanced.t's three `((?^:\v))` rows
are exactly that, and nothing else in either file moved.

WHAT THIS DOES TO OPTION (b).  The population is now SEVEN files and 2,070
blessed rows outside the row gate (op/hash.t 486, op/inc.t 36, op/undef.t 55,
op/utfhash.t 51 + re/pat.t 527, re/pat_advanced.t 515,
re/regexp_unicode_prop.t 396).  And the three new members sharpen the argument:
their volatility is NOT a description that quotes hash internals, it is the row
ORDER, which `PERL_HASH_SEED=0 PERL_PERTURB_KEYS=0` in the perl ORACLE child
would fix outright — and unlike op/hash.t, none of these three is a test OF hash
quality, so freezing the seed costs them nothing.  A third option is now also
visible: make `PclTapAlign::align_taps` pair equal descriptions as a MULTISET
rather than positionally within a 20-row window, which would fix all seven —
but that is the shared pairing behind FIXTURE, #185 expected-rows and I1, so it
needs its own session and a before/after verdict diff of all 111 registered
files (the same bar #1051 sets for the cap).  NOT taken here.
subject: Four companion files' ROW keys are nondeterministic: perl interpolates its own HASH ORDER into the test description, so the I1 multiset draws differently every run (registered *rows-unstable* s468be)
